how.eq: Forecast = non-usage charges booked this month + (usage cost month to date ÷ days elapsed) × days in month
how.d: Fixed charges (subscriptions, commitments, support) are counted once; usage is projected at its average daily rate so far. Closed months use actual cost. Computed per cost center, then added up.
Command Center: over budget above 0%, at risk within 3% of budget. Budgets & Forecasts: warning above +2%, critical above +5%.
A straight-line view of the current month, not a seasonal model. Board Pack program run-rates use spend to date ÷ days in the data window × 365.

how.eq: Confidence = mean(share of month elapsed, share of spend from live adapters, allocation coverage, share of closed invoice lines that tie out)
how.d: Rises as the month progresses and as more spend comes from live feeds that reconcile to invoices. Each input is shown next to the score.

how.eq:
Build work on an open work order with a threshold date → 107 → in service: 351.2 Transmission, 363.2 Distribution, 397.2 General or multi-function → 403 depreciation (Cr 108)
Recurring cloud and SaaS fees → functional O&M: Transmission 560, 561.1–561.3, 561.5–561.7, 566; Distribution 580–588; A&G 921, 923, 930.2; renewals and support 569.2, 592.3, 935.2
how.d: Rules are applied in order: tax, credits and corrections (R12, R13), commitment purchases (R9), capital (R1–R3, only with a valid work order), maintenance (R4), functional O&M (R5–R8); anything unresolved goes to the exception queue. Every ledger line carries the rule that placed it, its citation and its basis: Regulation where FERC text decides, [POLICY] where the controller signs it off (awaiting sign-off until then). Tax follows its line; a credit reverses to the original account. 920 is A&G salaries only, and a test blocks any cloud or SaaS invoice line from it.

how.eq:
457.1 direct = lines resolved to one company by tag or a fixed-entity policy
457.2 indirect = the rest × the receiving company's share of an approved factor
Direct share = 457.1 ÷ (457.1 + 457.2)
how.d: Direct charging comes first. Factors are employees, workstations, retail customers, transmission pole miles and GL transactions, by month. Each bill line carries the receiving company's own account by function.

how.eq:
Coverage = taggable spend with a valid value ÷ taggable spend, per required tag
Suspense share = untagged cost-center spend ÷ AWS and Azure usage in the period
how.d: Weighted by cost, by company and business unit. Spend with no valid operating company or cost center waits in suspense at the service company with an owner and an age; it is not spread into Corporate IT. Tax, credits, support, rounding and Marketplace purchases cannot be tagged and are reported apart.

how.eq:
107 balance = additions on a valid work order since the threshold date − transfers to plant
Monthly 403 = plant balance × approved depreciation rate ÷ 12
how.d: A capitalized line with no work order (no_work_order), or on a work order with no probable-to-complete date (capitalizable_without_threshold_date), is held out of 107 and expensed until fixed. Existing depreciation rates continue until the next depreciation case.

how.eq: Rate year = test-period actuals, annualized, + renewal escalators landing in the rate year
how.d: Built by vendor for the docket's operating company and jurisdiction (UT-05). Renewals and escalators come from the vendor register (UT-06). An invoice exception is flagged because it weakens the support.

There is no machine-learning model and no language model in any figure. Every projection is a fixed formula over billed data, so the same data always gives the same answer, and each figure shows its formula.

how.eq:
Sub-account spike: daily cost > 3 × its average over the prior 14 days, and > $500
API key spike: daily cost > 3σ above its trailing 14-day mean, and > $25
Copilot Studio surge: daily credits ≥ 3 × trailing 7-day average
how.d: Rules run over every day in the data. The excess above the baseline is reported as already spent.

how.eq:
Commitment-eligible spend × 28% (assumed Savings Plan discount)
Standard-tier AI cost × 50% (batch discount)
Idle seats = seat price of seats with no activity in 28 days
how.d: Estimates are opportunities, not savings. They stay labelled as estimates until verified.

how.eq: Verified = 30-day run-rate before the change − run-rate after (14+ days of data)
how.d: Measured on the scope that changed. With less than 14 days of data the estimate is shown as provisional.

how.eq:
Test-period spend failing the reconciliation, approved-policy, FERC-account or used-and-useful tests
+ unused share of seat purchases
+ share of a line equal to a savings estimate left unactioned for 60+ days
how.d: Evidence score = cost-weighted share of evidence present. Decision support for the regulatory team, not a prediction of any commission's order.

how.eq:
Earnings unlock = average regulatory-asset balance × the docket's pre-tax rate of return
Balance = annualized test-period recurring cloud and SaaS fees ÷ 12 × (amortization months + 1) ÷ 2
how.d: Over the contract term (62 months when none). Unlock covers jurisdictions where an order could allow deferral to 182.3 and none is on file; balances already deferred under an order earn their return today.

The CostIQ Summary page, and the agent's briefing, are written from the figures on the pages your role can open. CostIQ ranks what matters (forecast against budget, disallowance at risk, earnings unlock, open savings, NERC CIP and data findings, alerts and invoice exceptions) and writes one sentence per point. Every figure links to the panel or row it comes from, and the numbered chips list the source pages.

Your question is matched to one of the tested use cases by keyword ranking (BM25), parameters such as periods and providers are read from the text, and the use case runs in your scope. Nothing is generated; if nothing matches, CostIQ says so.

terms: The FinOps Foundation's open billing standard. Every provider's bill is loaded into the same FOCUS columns, so AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake and AI vendors compare line for line.
What the invoice charges for a line.
Cost after discounts and with commitment purchases spread over the usage they cover. Most CostIQ figures use it.
Price at public rates / at your negotiated rates. List − contracted = negotiated discount.
Savings Plan, reservation, committed-use discount or provisioned AI throughput (PTU) paid for in advance. Unused commitment is cost with no usage behind it.
Spend projected to a year from a recent period.
Where cost is reported, from tags, approved allocation rules or split-cost data. Each person sees only their own.
An approved, effective-dated rule that splits shared cost by a factor (for example retail customers or transmission pole miles). One person submits, another approves.
The company in the group that bears a cost (the service company, an operating company, a transmission company or the non-utility affiliate), and the state or FERC jurisdiction whose rates it reaches.
Technology cost the service company bills to each associate company at cost: 457.1 direct, 457.2 by an approved factor. Each bill line carries the receiving company's account.
Spend with no valid operating company or cost center. It waits at the service company with an owner and an age until it is tagged or restated through an approved rule.
cwip (construction work in progress, 107, on a valid work order), regulatory_asset (182.3, only with a commission order) or om (functional O&M).

The account a line is booked to under the Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101; Part 367 at the service company). Every ledger line carries the rule ID, citation and policy flag that placed it.

Since 2025-01-01, software placed in service is plant in 351.2 (Transmission), 363.2 (Distribution) or 397.2 (General or multi-function), depreciated through 403 (Cr 108). 303 stays for older balances and service-company software.
Implementation work on an open work order with a probable-to-complete (threshold) date is construction work in progress (107) until the module is ready for use, then moves to plant.

Recurring cloud and SaaS fees go to the O&M accounts of the function they serve: Transmission 560, 561.1–561.3, 561.5–561.7, 566 (never 561.4 or 561.8); Distribution 580–588; A&G 921, 923, 930.2; renewals and support 569.2, 592.3, 935.2. 920 is A&G salaries only.
Regulation: FERC text decides the placement. [POLICY]: FERC leaves the choice to the company, so the rule shows awaiting sign-off until the controller signs it off.
The actual period a rate case rests on, and the year rates are set for.
A rate case or other proceeding before a commission, with its own test period and filing date.

A question from commission staff or an intervenor. CostIQ drafts the answer from a tested use case, such as every transaction in an account with vendor, description and amount; someone else approves it.
A ZIP of the docket's evidence. Its SHA-256 fingerprint is sealed in the decision ledger, so anyone can check it later.
Test-period spend a commission could challenge because evidence is missing. Decision support, not a prediction of any order.
The return on cloud and SaaS costs that could be deferred to a regulatory asset where a commission order allows it.
Money already spent on waste or error (spikes, idle capacity, invoice mismatches).
A saving that has not happened yet. Never added to verified savings.
Spend on a workload that fails a compliance check. Reported separately; never summed with savings.
Identified → approved → implemented → verified, with a different person signing each step.

NERC's Critical Infrastructure Protection standards. They apply to the registered entity, not to tools or vendors. CostIQ flags and masks names on CIP-related accounts; the client's CIP program decides what is BES Cyber System Information (BCSI).
Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information, such as planning data. Flagged workloads are checked for where they are served.
Non-utility affiliate work carried by a regulated company. Control C-09 flags it so it can be retagged and the months restated.
Encryption keys the company controls, so the provider cannot read the data.
AI summarization cost ÷ customer contacts handled in the month.
The rules and the ledger delivered as SQL and a dbt project in the client's own Git repository, designed to run inside the client's Snowflake. The CostIQ app is optional.
Whoever submits a finding, policy, optimization or data-request response cannot approve or verify it.
A hash-chained log of every approval. Changing an old entry breaks the chain, which the Governance page checks.
A tested, named analysis with its SQL and formula. CostIQ runs more than 150 of them.
In CostIQ: computed from data CostIQ holds. Partial: part of the section needs a feed or an approval. Needs data: the missing input is named; nothing is estimated in its place.
